title: Open Hospital HMI Maintenance Menu and select maintenance functions (Manual Control, IO Diagnostics, Persistent Variables, Default)
summary: On the Hospital HMI / lane UI, open the “Maintenance Menu” screen and use its four buttons to navigate to the selected maintenance function screen: 2.1 Manual Control, 2.2 IO Diagnostics, 2.3 Persistent Variables, or 2.4 Default.
when_to_use: Use when you need to navigate the Hospital HMI Maintenance Menu to reach a specific maintenance function screen (Manual Control, IO Diagnostics, Persistent Variables, or Default).
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Navigate the Hospital HMI to the Maintenance Menu and select the desired maintenance function button.

visual_references.description: Hospital HMI Maintenance Menu screen showing four buttons: 2.1 Manual Control, 2.2 IO Diagnostics, 2.3 Persistent Variables, 2.4 Default.
Hospital HMI 2.2 IO Diagnostics screen (switch input states; HMI temperature and voltage readings).
Hospital HMI 2.4 Default screen (software info; Hospital Station IP address; login/logout; REBOOT TO SETUP for maintenance personnel).

steps.title: Open the Hospital HMI Maintenance Menu screen
steps.purpose: Get to the screen that contains the four maintenance function navigation buttons.
steps.instruction: On the Hospital HMI / lane UI, navigate to the “Maintenance Menu” screen.
steps.expected_result: The Hospital HMI shows the “Maintenance Menu” screen.
steps.healthy_condition: The “Maintenance Menu” screen is visible and ready for button selection.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot reach the “Maintenance Menu” screen (or the screen shown is not the Maintenance Menu).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The “Maintenance Menu” has four buttons that allow access to a variety of information: 2.1 Manual Control, 2.2 IO Diagnostics, 2.3 Persistent Variables, 2.4 Default.

steps.title: Verify the Maintenance Menu shows four labeled buttons
steps.purpose: Confirm the correct Maintenance Menu screen is displayed before selecting a function.
steps.instruction: Check that the Maintenance Menu screen shows exactly these four buttons: “2.1 Manual Control”, “2.2 IO Diagnostics”, “2.3 Persistent Variables”, and “2.4 Default”.
steps.expected_result: All four buttons are present with the exact labels 2.1, 2.2, 2.3, and 2.4 as shown on the Maintenance Menu.
steps.healthy_condition: The Maintenance Menu displays all four labeled buttons.
steps.failure_condition: The Maintenance Menu does not show all four buttons, or the labels do not match the expected 2.1/2.2/2.3/2.4 set.

actions.label: Confirm button labels
actions.exact_action: Verify the Maintenance Menu screen shows exactly four buttons: “2.1 Manual Control”, “2.2 IO Diagnostics”, “2.3 Persistent Variables”, and “2.4 Default”.

stop_or_escalate_if: If the Maintenance Menu screen does not show all four buttons, stop and escalate to FORTNA support for further troubleshooting.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The “Maintenance Menu” has four buttons that allow access to a variety of information: 2.1 Manual Control, 2.2 IO Diagnostics, 2.3 Persistent Variables, 2.4 Default.

steps.title: Select the desired maintenance function button
steps.purpose: Open the selected maintenance function screen from the Maintenance Menu.
steps.instruction: Click the desired button on the Maintenance Menu: Manual Control (2.1), IO Diagnostics (2.2), Persistent Variables (2.3), or Default (2.4).
steps.expected_result: The Hospital HMI screen changes away from the Maintenance Menu and opens the corresponding maintenance function screen for the selected button.
steps.healthy_condition: After clicking a button, the UI transitions to the next maintenance screen (the Maintenance Menu buttons are no longer shown).
steps.failure_condition: After clicking the selected button, the screen does not change (or it does not open the corresponding maintenance function screen).

actions.label: Click maintenance function button
actions.exact_action: Click the desired button (Manual Control, IO Diagnostics, Persistent Variables, or Default) to open the corresponding maintenance function screen.

stop_or_escalate_if: If the selected button does not change screens, stop and escalate to FORTNA support for further troubleshooting.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The “Maintenance Menu” has four buttons that allow access to a variety of information: 2.1 Manual Control, 2.2 IO Diagnostics, 2.3 Persistent Variables, 2.4 Default.

steps.title: Confirm the screen transitioned to the selected maintenance function
steps.purpose: Ensure the correct maintenance function screen opened for the selected button.
steps.instruction: Confirm the Hospital HMI no longer shows the Maintenance Menu buttons and instead shows the maintenance function screen corresponding to the button you selected.
steps.expected_result: The UI displays the selected maintenance function screen (Manual Control / IO Diagnostics / Persistent Variables / Default).
steps.healthy_condition: The Maintenance Menu buttons are replaced by the selected function’s screen content.
steps.failure_condition: The Maintenance Menu buttons remain visible, or the displayed screen does not correspond to the selected function.

actions.label: Check destination screen
actions.exact_action: Confirm the screen changes to the selected maintenance function (i.e., the UI no longer shows the Maintenance Menu buttons and instead shows the next maintenance screen for the selected function).

stop_or_escalate_if: If the screen does not transition correctly to the selected maintenance function, stop and escalate to FORTNA support for further troubleshooting.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The “IO Diagnostics” screen corresponds to the switch mounted on the station and conveys which inputs are on and off; temperature readings and voltages pertain to the HMI itself.

The “Default” screen displays information related to the software currently installed and the IP address of the Hospital Station; users can log in and log out; only maintenance personnel should use the REBOOT TO SETUP button if they need to update the date or time on the HMI.

success_criteria: The Hospital HMI Maintenance Menu displays four labeled buttons: 2.1 Manual Control, 2.2 IO Diagnostics, 2.3 Persistent Variables, and 2.4 Default.
Selecting any of the four buttons transitions the UI away from the Maintenance Menu to the corresponding maintenance function screen.
healthy_conditions: Maintenance Menu screen shows exactly four buttons with labels 2.1 Manual Control, 2.2 IO Diagnostics, 2.3 Persistent Variables, 2.4 Default.
After selecting a button, the Maintenance Menu buttons are no longer shown and the corresponding maintenance function screen is displayed.
failure_conditions: Maintenance Menu screen does not show all four buttons.
Selected button does not change screens.
Displayed destination screen does not correspond to the selected maintenance function.
escalation_guidance: If the Maintenance Menu does not show all four buttons or the selected button does not change screens, stop and escalate to FORTNA support for further troubleshooting.
missing_details: The packet does not include destination UI details for 2.1 Manual Control and 2.3 Persistent Variables; this runbook only verifies that the screen transitions away from the Maintenance Menu and provides optional evidence for 2.2 IO Diagnostics and 2.4 Default.
